title: Check yourself: Judging the output and owning the result

questions.stem: An analyst asks Claude to summarise a regulation for compliance colleagues. The summary cites "subsection 14(b)(ii)" for a retention rule, and the analyst is about to forward it. What is the most appropriate step?

options.text: Ask Claude whether it is confident, and forward the summary if it says yes
options.says: Ruled out because the routine says that asking the model how sure it is, or "for its confidence does not verify anything".

options.text: Look the passage up in the source of record before the text goes out
options.says: Specific citations are the kind of detail a model can invent, so the claim that would hurt if wrong is checked against the source of record (the checking routine).

options.text: Ask Claude to cite the subsection again in a fresh reply and compare the two
options.says: Ruled out because the routine says to check "against the source of record, not against the model", and a second reply from the same model is not the source.

options.text: Forward it with a note that an AI drafted it, so readers can judge
options.says: Ruled out because "Check in proportion to the cost of being wrong", and a note about an AI draft leaves the unchecked claim in place.

questions.stem: A competitor table has one cell marked "data unavailable" while every other cell is filled. A colleague asks you to drop that row so the table looks finished. Which response is best?

options.text: Ask Claude to try again until every cell holds a value
options.says: Ruled out because "Regenerating the same request and hoping is the reflex", and pressing for a value invites invention.

options.text: Fill it with a typical industry figure and label it an estimate
options.says: Ruled out because "the careless move is to fill the gap with an estimate".

options.text: Show a dash in that cell and drop any mention of the missing data
options.says: Ruled out because the page says "Keep the gap and decide what to do about it", not hide it behind a dash.

options.text: Retain the entry as it stands and state what could not be located
options.says: A declared gap is information, and the careful move is to keep it and decide what to do (the spotting a gap section).
